statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r)=2. The first component r[0] contains exactly, with no repetitions and in arbitrary order, those edge indices i with 0 <= i < m that belong to every minimum spanning tree of G. The second component r[1] contains exactly, with no repetitions and in arbitrary order, those edge indices i with 0 <= i < m for which there exists a minimum spanning tree of G containing i and there also exists a minimum spanning tree of G not containing i. No other integers occur in either component. Here a minimum spanning tree means a subset T of the edge indices forming a connected acyclic spanning subgraph of G whose total weight sum_{i in T} w_i is minimal.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 100; edges has length m with 1 <= m <= min(200, n*(n-1)/2); for every i with 0 <= i < m, edges[i] has length 3, and, writing a_i=edges[i][0], b_i=edges[i][1], w_i=edges[i][2], we have 0 <= a_i < b_i < n and 1 <= w_i <= 1000; all unordered pairs {a_i,b_i} are distinct; the undirected graph G on vertices {0,...,n-1} with edge i joining a_i and b_i is connected.
